ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: start here
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What Rimfolk adds to your colony, and where to find it.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: You don't need all of it on the first day. Answer the wishes and see what the colonists do.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
Rimfolk turns your colonists into a small society. They ask for things and remember what you did about it, make friends and rivals, keep journals, dream, and wear down under hard times. A council helps you keep up: an advisor that points out what the colony needs, and meetings where the colony picks a goal to work toward.
All of it lives in four windows, one button each on the bottom bar: council (the colony's own life in four views: This week, People, Council and Colony), region (the region map read through its lenses, the peoples and their faces, who is here and who is away, and the history), defense, and planning (the plan with the advisor's priorities, the base, making and the rooms). Each window has the four in its top right corner, so you can go from one to another, and before them a back and a forward arrow that retrace where you were across all four, a magnifying glass that finds anyone and anything by name, This week's tray with the count of what waits on you, a pin with what you follow, and a book that opens this Almanac in a window of its own. The council window comes back to the view you were last on (the mod settings can make it always open on This week, the view of what needs you); the region window opens on its map. The windows open at 1010 by 720; on a large screen the setting "Window size" (Interface) lets them grow up to 1280 by 860.

points.li: Start each day on This week (the council window's first view), the one place where everything waits on you. Following has what you follow. Needs you has wishes and petitions, oldest first, letters that want an answer, a hamlet's or a raiders' camp's ask, a debt called in and promises at risk, each with its act on the right (Answer, Decide, Look, Pay). Under way has letters on the road, caravans, missions taken on and settlers, each shown by the step it is at (written, on the road, arrived, answered). Coming has the calendar's days, fights promised and missions offered, by the day they come. Then how people are (strain, serious illness, trust, the balance of Rimfolk's moods) and the plan's two most pressing steps. Click a line to go where it leads, or a name in it for its card; "and 3 more" opens the rest in place. The number of things that wait on you is the same on This week's tab, in every window's corner and on the council button.
Look at the priorities (the planning window, Plan, then Priorities) now and then. They list what the colony needs, worst first, beside the plan you act on.
Answer wishes as they come. Grant one by making it happen, promise it to buy time, or refuse it. A refusal costs less than a wish left to lapse.

Select a colonist and open their Mood tab to see what weighs on them and what would help, their Story tab for who they are and what they've lived, their Culture tab for what they believe and where they come from, or the game's Social tab, where Rimfolk's column on the right shows their bonds, groups, name, shared memories, talks and secrets.
About once a quadrum the council meets in the evening. Keep people at home that day if their say matters to you.

The smaller news (new friends, quirks, birthdays, ailments, a story moving on) comes together in one Colony news letter each evening, with a button to go where each happened. Letters that ask you to decide, and serious news, still come at once; the Colony news setting can show it all as it happens instead, or send it only to the History tab. Rimfolk weighs each thing it tells by how much it matters and how busy the day already is: past the day's share of messages and letters for the colony (in the settings, under Messages), or for one person's news, their health and the land's on a busy day (after a raid or something serious), they wait for that evening letter too, and the same thing twice within a few hours is told once. The evening letter carries fewer lines the busier the day was, the ones that matter most, and the rest go to the History tab. With more than one colony, each names the settlement it comes from.

li.heading: Finding your way around the council window

points.li: The council window's four views, in one row of tabs: This week (what waits on you), People (the table of everyone, moods, bonds, ideoligions, renown), Council (offices and decrees with the elections, the ambition and its meetings, our ways, wishes and petitions, dilemmas) and Colony (the overview, the calendar, the chronicle). The small buttons under a view's title are its modes, other ways of showing the same things; the "?" right of its title opens its page of this Almanac, in a window of its own that you can move and size beside what it explains.

People, then Table: every colonist in one table, with mood and Rimfolk's share of it, trust and how it moved this week, strain, the setbacks weighing on them and what helps, their wish, their personal story, health and quirks. Click a heading to sort; hover a cell for more; click a row to open the colonist's card beside the table, with their whole story, their dreams and the newest lines of their journal. Every dream and every journal is in Colony, then Chronicle, under the Dreams and Journals filters; People, then Renown has the colony's name among the peoples and its people known by name.
Council, then Dilemmas: the questions waiting for an answer, the traditions the answers founded, and every answer since with how it went.

The region window has four views. Map: the region map, read through six lenses along its top (Land; Stance and ties, with a line from home for each tie; Fortunes; Threats, with the raiders' camps and the fights on their way; Trade, with the trading posts; Ours, with the colony's homes, hamlets and caravans), each with its legend at the map's foot and a List of what it shows, nearest first. Peoples: each people, how it stands with the colony, its wars, what is owed each way and what it remembers; its Faces mode has the people you know by name, with a way to write, the colony's old foes and those who left. Here and away: who is here from outside (a camp on your land, guests), what is on its way, letters on the road, who of yours is away (journeys and caravans), missions and the colony's houses. History: the world's history, for this colony, the region or the whole world, with the world's events running in a strip at its top, letters lately, and filters for a people, a town or a kind of event. The old pages' names still lead there.

Names in Rimfolk's four windows lead somewhere, and so do the names in the Story, Culture and Mood tabs and the Social tab's column. A name drawn in parchment with a dotted line under it is a link: click it and its card opens in the drawer at the right of the window, beside what you were looking at. A card has the same parts for everyone and everything (a colonist, someone out in the world, a town or another place, a people, a family, a debt or another tie, an entry of the history, a letter): what is happening now, its people, its ties, what was said, its story with a link to its whole history, and what the colony can do, each act greyed with the reason when it can't be done. On the region map the drawer is the map's panel: picking a town opens its card there, and the small world button on a place's card still shows it in the game's world view. Escape closes the drawer before the window.

Rest the mouse on a name for a moment and a small preview says who or what it is; move into it to keep it open, rest on a name inside it for one more preview beside it, and click it to open the card. The settings under "Names and cards" set the pause or turn previews off. Back and forward retrace the pages, filters and cards you opened (up to 50 steps); Options, then Keyboard, has two keys for them under "Rimfolk", and a mouse's side buttons work too where the system reports them. "Show" in the region map's lists, on Here and away and on This week opens the place on the region map with its card. From a colonist's tabs or a panel, a name opens its card in a small window of its own, with a button to open it in its window.

Every window reads the same way. A colour always means one thing and always sits beside its word or its icon: green for friendly or well, slate blue for neutral or under way, red for hostile or bad, orange for what needs you soon, a brighter red with the warning sign for harm now, a muted green for what is done or kept, gold for the colony's own and what it chose, pale blue for news from afar. A section's heading carries its count, a tag is a dot and a word, a short line of the last week sits beside the overview's numbers and the colony's mood, and an act that can't be done now is greyed with the reason as its tooltip and, in a card, a line under it. On the screen's panels (moods, health, work and idle, what you follow) a colonist's name is a link too: a click on the name opens their card, and the rest of the row still takes you to them on the map; the hover card's name is one when the card sits in the corner.

The defense window: where raiders can reach you from on this map, the narrow places on their way and how many raids pass each, what you face and what stands already, advice on what to build first with the reasons for it, and defense plans (a gate with sandbags, a killbox, a palisade with a gatehouse...) to place like room plans, at the spot the council suggests and facing the raiders. "Show on the map" draws the ways in. Like the other windows it has a "?" to its page of this Almanac, sections that fold, and the card of anyone named there in the drawer at its right.

The planning window, in four views: Plan (the colony's next steps, and as its second mode the advisor's priorities, worst first, which share its "Not this"), Base (the base looked over), Making (what you could make) and Rooms (the room plans as a list, or every room at a glance as the rooms button used to show them).

Follow anyone or anything with the pin on its card's head (a colonist, someone out in the world, a town, a people, a family, a debt): up to twelve show at the top of This week, each with its newest change in one line, and in the Following panel on the screen if you switch it on (the pin in the corner lists them and has the switch). The pin also shows when you hover a colonist's line on This week or a row in the People table; a wish card's pin keeps the wish there too.

The magnifying glass in the corner (or its key, under "Rimfolk" in Options, then Keyboard) finds colonists, people outside, places, peoples, the windows' views ("Bonds") and this Almanac's pages by name, grouped by kind; Enter opens the first, the arrows pick another.
"Put away" on This week's news line (or "Put all news away" in a news letter) clears the evenings' colony news from the letter stack; it stays in the History tab.
Each page remembers its filter and sort order. Options, then Keyboard, has optional shortcuts for the pages of Rimfolk's windows under "Rimfolk"; none is set until you pick a key.

li.heading: Too much at once?
li.text: Every part has its own switch in the mod settings (Options, then Mod options, then Rimfolk), on seven pages with a search box over them, and a line under each switch says what you'll notice with it on. Four presets set many at once: light touch, story-rich, demanding and default, each listing what it changes before it does. The Stakes setting decides how much it all matters: Gentle has only upsides, and Advisor only has no mood effects at all.

li.heading: Reading on
li.text:
The pages below explain the main parts. Each one ends with its own links, like this page.
If the text is too small or too cramped, the Aa buttons at the top of the almanac set its text size (Small, Normal, Large or Larger, also in the mod settings), and the « button beside them folds the lists away so a page gets the whole width. Tables too wide for the page show each row as a small card. The Almanac's window moves and sizes like any other, and a page you come back to opens where you left it.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: checking that it works
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Where to look to see each of the newer features at work.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Most of these wait for their moment: a happy colonist, a long day of hauling, an evening meeting.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: A short list for checking that Rimfolk's newer parts are running in your game. Each one says where to look and what you should see. Most need their setting on, and a few need the deeper game hooks.

points.li: Good times: open the Mood tab of a happy colonist (above 75% mood). Under their moods, a faint "Good times" line says what Rimfolk's balance takes off their good moods right now. Hover it for the rules.

Ailments: after a long day of hauling, mining or building, a colonist now and then gets a strained back, and after long bench work sore hands. It shows in their Health tab, and its description says what helps. The game's disease events also bring head colds and stomach bugs.

Visual touches: on a comet night the sky takes a faint cool cast, firefly nights bring small green-gold blinks around colonists outside after dark, and a council meeting opens with a bell. Only on the map you're looking at.

Meetings: on the Ambition page, call a council meeting. At the set time colonists put down their work and walk over, and sleepers are woken and come late. The letter at the end says who came, who was late and who missed it, and why.
The heart in RimHUD: in RimHUD's settings, Content tab, "Add third-party" lists Rimfolk's lines (strain, feelings, the heart's needs) and bars. Once added, they show in a colonist's RimHUD panel.

Personal stories: once one begins (a message names it), the colonist's Story tab shows it near the top, with a dot for each stage; hover it for the stage it has reached and what it waits for next. Each stage adds a journal line and a chronicle line; a talk the story waits on shows in the social log. In development mode, "Personal story: begin one for..." starts one for a colonist it fits, and "Personal story: next stage" moves it on.

The colony calendar: open Colony, then Calendar. Founding day is there from the start, and long-serving colonists' birthdays after two years. Name a day for today with "Name a day": within the hour (in the daytime) its letter comes, and keeping it starts a party, games or a rest day.

Material counts: open a room plan and look at its materials. Each shows green with some to spare and amber when it only just covers the room. In the game's build menu, a wall's material list reads like "Steel wall 420 (+85 lying around), enough for 84".

What colonists say: keep the camera on the colony for a few hours. Now and then someone says a short line over their head about how they are: a strong feeling (the heart section of their Mood tab says which), an ailment from their Health tab, a setback from their Mood tab, a calendar day tomorrow, a wish still open. The same colonist speaks about once a day at most. It shows as the setting "Colonists' speech shows as" says: speech bubbles with Interaction Bubbles, else floating text.

Gatherings: at a bonfire the fire smokes, and sparks after dark; at a toast, a while in, a small warm glint goes up over every head at once; at a grave after dark, while someone remembers there, a low warm glow shows by the stone. A calendar day's letter is followed by a small bell.

Small habits: after a death, watch the one who grieves in their free time; the job line in their inspect pane reads "visiting (name)'s grave". A convalescent's reads "taking a slow walk", and after a raid the ones who fought may be "sitting by the fire after the fight" if the colony has a lit campfire. A lonely colonist (the heart section of the Mood tab says so) may be "keeping (name) company", a worried one "going over the stores", a nostalgic one "telling old stories by the fire" of an evening, and one awed by something, or who watches the stars, "watching the stars" on a clear night. On a cold day, with a sauna in the colony (a small hot room with a seat, or Dubs Bad Hygiene's), someone with time to spare may be "sitting in the sauna".

Rimfolk's events on the map: a camp walking in raises a little dust on the road, and someone who sees them come says so; the first hours of the first snow catch a few flakes on the colonists out in it; the morning after a dream, the dreamer at breakfast tells it over the bowl; and a wedding the council promised (or of one of its officers) is rung in with a small bell and a word from a councillor. With Hospitality, a guest on screen now and then says something about their stay.

The weather: when the first snow of a winter falls (after ten days or more without any), a heat wave or cold snap begins, or a storm rolls in, someone in view says something about it, and a line may turn up in a journal. In the two days after the first snow, children may go out to build snowmen. After a few weeks the Overview page has a Weather card with this season against last year's and the colony's records. On a bitter morning breath shows at the mouths of colonists outside, and Rimfolk's hail is seen coming in a green sky two hours before it falls.

Badges on the colonist bar: as a colonist's mood sinks toward their minor break line, a faint amber ring shows around their portrait at the top of the screen, turning orange and then red as it falls. A wish that has waited past half its time puts a small speech bubble in the portrait's top right corner: hover it for what it means, click it for the Wishes page.

li.heading: When something doesn't show
li.text:
Check its setting first. Then turn on development mode (Options), open the debug actions and pick "Rimfolk: check myself" under Rimfolk. It lists which game hooks took, which parts are switched on and which of your mods Rimfolk found, and says whether a camp or a trade caravan could come now and what stops it. For the slower stories it says which regulars the colony keeps up with and whether one could come back, who leads the herd, what the beast that stays is up to or what stands between a wild animal and a name, and whether a shiny rumour holds. A screenshot of it says a lot in a bug report.
Development mode also has shortcuts for testing: "Heart: add 20 strain" moves a colonist's strain bar, the comet and firefly nights can be started from the incident list, and "Calendar: a day comes round now" brings any day on the calendar round at once.
